title: Subnet discovery is on by default from v1.18 — secondary ENIs can land in other subnets tagged kubernetes.io/role/cni

detection.reason: ENABLE_SUBNET_DISCOVERY's VALUE is not collected; subnet tags and the node role's IAM policy are AWS-side

remediation: From v1.18 ipamd picks, per new secondary ENI, the subnet with the most free IPs among the node's own subnet and subnets in its VPC/AZ tagged kubernetes.io/role/cni (ENABLE_SUBNET_DISCOVERY defaults to true). Pods can therefore get IPs from those subnets — check their route tables, NACLs and security-group expectations — and the CNI role needs ec2:DescribeSubnets (without it discovery falls back to the node's subnet). Set ENABLE_SUBNET_DISCOVERY=false to keep the old behaviour.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get ds aws-node -o json | jq -r '.spec.template.spec.containers[] | .name as $c | .env[]? | select(.name | test("^(ENABLE_SUBNET_DISCOVERY)$")) | "\($c): \(.name)=\(.value // "(from \(.valueFrom | keys | join(",")))")"'  # absent or true = discovery on: subnets tagged kubernetes.io/role/cni in the node's VPC/AZ can host pod IPs
coversNotes: Bugfix - updating iam doc with subnet policy

title: awscni_no_available_ip_addresses becomes a counter (v1.18.1) — gauge-style alerts misfire

detection.reason: alert rules and dashboards that query the metric are outside the cluster objects collected

quote: Switch to counter type metic for awscni_no_available_ip_addresses
remediation: awscni_no_available_ip_addresses is a monotonically increasing counter from v1.18.1: an alert written as `awscni_no_available_ip_addresses > 0` fires forever after the first failed IP assignment. Rewrite it as `increase(awscni_no_available_ip_addresses[10m]) > 0`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get prometheusrules -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(tostring | test("awscni_no_available_ip_addresses")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each PrometheusRule printed queries the metric; check it uses rate()/increase(), not a raw threshold

title: The ENIConfig CRD gains a schema (v1.18.3): spec.subnet becomes required, unknown spec fields are pruned

detection.reason: ENIConfig objects are not collected yet

quote: Update the APISpec Schema definition for ENIConfig.
remediation: After the CRD from the v1.18.3+ chart/manifest is applied, the API server validates ENIConfigs: an ENIConfig without spec.subnet is rejected on its next write, and spec fields other than subnet/securityGroups are pruned. Fix such objects before applying the new CRD.
verifyCommand: kubectl get eniconfigs -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select((.spec.subnet // "") == "" or ((.spec | keys) - ["subnet","securityGroups"] | length) != 0) | .metadata.name'  # each ENIConfig printed lacks spec.subnet or carries spec fields the v1.18.3 schema prunes
